title: Frugal session prototype jot
content:
Context: rough personal notebook for a tiny feature seed — want a low-effort, high-impact way to offer tiered response fidelity per session so apps can trade cost for quality dynamically. Not a full PRD yet, more of a hypothesis + quick experiments list.

Problem statement:
- Customers want predictable token/unit spend for long-running conversational sessions (agents, assistants, customer support bots).
- Current model-level knobs (quantization, model size) are coarse; per-session fidelity adjustments require infra + UX work.
- Many apps would accept slightly shorter/less verbose responses in non-critical sessions to save 20–50% cost.

Hypothesis:
- If we expose a lightweight "session fidelity" tier (high/medium/eco) with small runtime transforms (compression, trimming, lexical pruning, concise generation prompts), customers can reduce hosting bill and maintain acceptable UX.

Goal (MVP):
- Prototype a session flag that signals the serving runtime + prompt orchestration layer to apply low-risk fidelity reductions.
- Keep changes minimal: no new model weights, no extra infra services. Evaluate cost delta and UX degradation.

Success metrics (initial):
- Synthetic: tokens-per-session reduction >= 20% on median for non-high sessions.
- Human eval: < 10% of responses judged "unacceptable" in a small 50-session panel.
- Product: 3 pilot customers opt into eco tier within 8 weeks.

Core ideas (ranked quick):
1) Micro-slate templates: short-format instruction templates plus a concise completion length cap. E.g., prepend system: "Answer concisely (1–3 bullets) unless user asks for detail."
2) Fractionated response pipeline: run a brief aggressive decode pass (eco) then allow an optional follow-up expansion if user requests more.
3) Prefix compression: automatically trim prior turns using simple heuristics (remove filler, summarize to 1–2 sentences) before sending to model when session fidelity != high.
4) Token-aware output filters: prefer enumerations and condensed grammar to avoid fluff.
5) KV cache reuse + micro-batching tweaks to keep latency stable when applying summarization transforms.

User stories (examples):
- As a mobile app developer, I want sessions marked "eco" so my free-tier users generate cheaper replies and stay within monthly credits.
- As a chatOps admin, I want to tag long-running background assistants as "medium" to cap costs without fully degrading quality.
- As an SRE, I want minimal additional CPU or latency impact from fidelity transforms.

Minimal API surface (MVP):
- session_fidelity: "high"|"medium"|"eco" in session metadata; default = high
- server behavior: if not high, apply templated prompt wrapper + max_tokens cap + optional summarization of history

Behavioral details to prototype:
- Eco: aggressive history summarization (max 100 tokens of context), shorter system template, max output tokens 80
- Medium: mild summarization (300 tokens), max output tokens 200, preserve full user turn that triggered current reply
- High: unchanged

Small experiments to run (week-by-week):
W1: implement session flag passthrough in API + simple template injection (no summarization). Run offline sampling across existing logs to measure token delta.
W2: add naive summarizer (rule-based clause removal + sentence-extractive summary) in edge proxy; measure latency and token reduction.
W3: human eval panel (50 sessions each fidelity) for acceptability judgments.
W4: iterate transforms: try short prompt-only approach vs extractive-summary-first.

Safety / risk notes:
- Don't do anything that removes user intent-critical tokens. For initial prototype, summarizer should be conservative (prefer leaving more than trimming).
- Logging & debugging: preserve original request shard in logs for audit and replays.
- Contract with SRE: cap CPU overhead to +10% p95 for edges doing summarization.

Metrics to collect (telemetry keys):
- tokens_in, tokens_out per session, per-turn
- generate_time (ms), summarization_time (ms), extra_cpu_seconds
- user_followups_per_response (proxy for insufficient answers)
- human_acceptability_score (from panel)

Rollout plan (sketch):
- internal beta (dev team) -> small pilot customers -> gradual rollout with opt-in UI and admin controls.

Open questions / parking lot:
- How to present fidelity to end-users? badge/labeling vs implicit? (privacy/UX tradeoffs)
- Fine-grained toggles: should we allow per-route defaults? per-user overrides?
- Could we monetize eco tier for freemium apps? pricing model thoughts later.
- Would this interact badly with function/tool calling? (probably need to default to high for tool flows)
- Interaction with rollouts: how to A/B across fidelity without confusing tracing?

Todo (next small actions):
- Spike: implement API passthrough + template injection (me) — deadline: 2026-02-28
- Ask Mika to prototype extractive summarizer in python microservice — pinged in Slack, follow up by 2026-02-25
- Draft simple pilot email for 3 customers (Omar)
- Add telemetry keys to infra schema (Lena)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this frictionless: most value is in requiring very little config from customers.
- Aim to reuse existing rollout hooks and tracing so we can measure per-fidelity impact quickly.
- If human eval looks bad, don't escalate quantization yet — try prompt-first approaches.

Misc quick links / refs I looked at:
- internal gist: one-shot-summaries (link in slack pinned)
- similar idea: "compact-response-allocator" doc (search drive)

End of jot. This is intentionally messy — main purpose: capture the seed and a 4-week experiment plan.
summary: Seed notes for a 'session fidelity' MVP to let customers choose cost/quality tiers per session. Includes hypothesis, quick MVP API, experiments, metrics, rollout sketch, and next steps.
